<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard sources from the project's GitHub repository, including documentation files and a prebuilt binary tarball for x86_64. The `source` array entries use HTTPS URLs pointing to the legitimate upstream (github.com/tareqmy/gitwig), and while checksums are provided, even if they were skipped (which they are not), that would not pose a risk during the `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` phase because the commands only fetch and extract sources without executing them.

The top-level scope contains only variable assignments and string expansions; there is no command substitution, external code execution, or network activity triggered during sourcing. The `pkgver` function is not defined, so the static `pkgver=2.5.13` is used, eliminating any risk of malicious code execution via dynamic version calculation. Functions like `prepare()` and `package()` are not executed due to the `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` flags, so their contents are out of scope for this safety gate.

All operations during the sourcing and source-fetching phase are limited to downloading files from the declared upstream over HTTPS and storing them locally. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, dynamic code evaluation, or execution of remote scripts during the PKGBUILD parse and source download stage.
</details>
